title: How to Get More Out of Granola Meeting Notes
summary: Get more out of Granola meeting notes with 7 practical tips, from better jotting to turning action items into a prioritized to-do list that updates itself.
body_markdown:
Granola meeting notes are some of the best around. Granola listens through your computer audio without a bot joining the call, combines what it hears with the few lines you type, and hands you clean, enhanced notes the moment the meeting ends.


But great notes are only half the job.


The real value of a meeting is in what happens after it: the follow-up email you promised, the numbers someone owes you, the decision that changes next week's plan. If those stay buried in a notes app you only open when you remember to, the meeting didn't really pay off.


Here's how to get more out of Granola, from small habits inside the app to connecting it with the rest of your work so action items actually get done.


## Key takeaways


-


Jot only what matters during the meeting and let Granola fill in the rest.


-


Pull action items and follow-ups out **before you close the notes** , not later.


-


Connect Granola to a tool like **BOND** so action items land in one prioritized to-do list alongside your email and Slack.


## 1. Jot less, but jot the right things


Granola works best when you treat it like a personal notepad, not a transcript. You don't need to capture everything, since it's transcribing in the background. Instead, type the few things only you know matter: a decision, a name, a number, "I owe Priya the deck."


Those short notes act as anchors. When Granola enhances your notes after the meeting, it builds around what you flagged, so the summary reflects your priorities rather than a neutral recap.


A good rule: if you'd be annoyed to forget it, type it.


## 2. Connect your calendar so every meeting is captured


Granola syncs with your calendar to spot upcoming meetings, and it works with Zoom, Google Meet, Teams and in-person conversations through its mobile apps. Connecting your calendar means fewer "I forgot to start it" moments.


It also unlocks Granola's pre-meeting briefs for external calls, covering who's attending and what you discussed before. Walking in with that context makes the meeting itself shorter and sharper.


## 3. Pull out action items before you close the notes


The most common way Granola meeting notes lose value: you read the summary, think "great," and close the window. The action items are in there, but now they're in a document instead of on a list.


Before you move on, spend 30 seconds on Granola's quick prompts to list action items and draft a follow-up. Check that every action item has an owner and a date. If it doesn't, that's a sign the meeting ended without a real decision, and it's worth a quick message to clarify.


For a full system for tracking these, see our guide on how to keep track of follow-ups at work.


## 4. Ask questions across meetings, not just one


Granola Chat can answer questions across all your meetings, not just the one in front of you. That's where it gets powerful for leaders. Try prompts like:


-


"What did I commit to this week?"


-


"What has the sales team said about pricing in the last month?"


-


"Which open questions came up in my last three one-on-ones with Sam?"


Start broad, then narrow down. You'll often find patterns, like the same blocker mentioned in four different meetings, that no single set of notes would show.


## 5. Send the follow-up while it's fresh


A follow-up sent within the hour gets a very different response from one sent three days later. Granola can draft a follow-up email from your notes right after the meeting. Edit it for tone, add anything it missed, and send it before your next call.


This also puts commitments in writing, which makes them much easier to track later.


## 6. Turn Granola action items into a prioritized to-do list with BOND


Here's the gap even the best note-taker leaves: action items from meetings live in Granola, while the rest of your work lives in email, Slack and your calendar. You end up with several to-do lists and no clear sense of what matters most today.


BOND connects to Granola, along with Gmail or Outlook, Calendar, Slack, Notion, Linear and other tools. It reads your meeting notes alongside everything else and pulls the commitments into a single self-updating to-do list, ranked P0 to P3. An action item from this morning's board prep sits next to the contract waiting in your inbox and the bug a teammate flagged in Slack, in order of what actually matters.


A few ways that plays out:


-


**Action items become tasks automatically.** You don't copy anything out of Granola. BOND picks up what you committed to and adds it to your list.


-


**"Waiting on" gets tracked too.** When someone in the meeting promises you something, BOND keeps track and flags it if it goes overdue.


-


**Follow-ups get drafted.** BOND drafts follow-ups in your voice using the context from your Granola call, so you only have to review and send.


-


**Priorities stay accurate.** Because BOND sees the full picture across your tools and learns your priorities over time, it can tell a passing comment from a real commitment and cut through the noise.


If you've wondered what an AI chief of staff actually does day to day, this is a big part of it.


## 7. Walk into the next meeting already prepared


Meeting notes are most valuable right before you meet the same people again. Before a recurring meeting or a one-on-one, review what was decided last time and what's still open.


Granola's briefs help with external meetings. BOND adds meeting briefs that combine past Granola notes with related emails, Slack threads and open tasks, and its morning brief shows what's on deck for the day. Two minutes of prep turns a status update into a real conversation.

It connects to Granola and the rest of your tools, turns action items and commitments into a prioritized, self-updating to-do list, and drafts follow-ups so nothing stalls between meetings. ## FAQ


**How do I get action items from Granola meeting notes?**


Use Granola's quick prompts or Granola Chat to list action items after the meeting, and check that each one has an owner and a due date. To get them onto a to-do list automatically, connect Granola to BOND, which pulls commitments from your notes into a prioritized list.


**Does Granola integrate with task managers?**


Granola offers an MCP connector so AI tools can access your meeting notes, and many work tools connect to it. BOND integrates with Granola directly and turns your notes into prioritized tasks alongside your email, Slack and calendar. For other options, see our roundup of the best AI to-do list apps.


**Does Granola join meetings as a bot?**


No. Granola captures audio from your computer, so no bot joins the call. It works with Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams and in-person meetings via its mobile apps.


**Is Granola free?**


Granola has a free tier with unlimited meeting notes. Notes older than 30 days require an upgrade to view and work with.


**How do I share Granola notes with my team?**


Granola notes are private by default, and you can choose to share them with meeting participants. For keeping your team aligned on what was decided, a written follow-up after the meeting is usually the clearest option.


**What's the best way to track follow-ups from meetings?**


Capture action items before the meeting ends, keep them in one place with owners and dates, and review them weekly. Our guide on[how to prioritize tasks when everything is P0](https://www.bondapp.io/insights/how-to-prioritize-tasks-when-everything-is-p0) helps when the list gets long.
